header.userPrompt: When a flow is run, do we check if there's an orca run in progress? As witnessed by a progress file, along with a matching branch name? If not, we should, and we should then report an error to the user. The error should include the original prompt, with which the flow was started, along with branch information. I guess the continue-interrupted-flow detection relies on the same mechanism? So then we could say to the user - use the interrupted flow option or change the branch. That said, we could print a status line on startup, next to the "agents" and "stack" information, on which branch we currently are. This could be printed above the user-selection whenever the orca menu is presented

resultJson.description:
Today, orca only detects an in-progress (interrupted) run when the user re-runs the flow with the byte-identical prompt: the progress log is keyed by a hash of the prompt, so `FlowLifecycle.setup` consults only the current prompt's own `.orca/progress-<hash>.json`. If a run was interrupted on its feature branch and the user starts a flow with a *different* prompt while still on that branch, orca silently treats it as a fresh run — branching off (or, in skip-branch mode, committing directly onto) the interrupted run's branch, mixing two runs' history. This epic makes that situation a hard, actionable error: before any tree mutation, a fresh run scans all progress logs, and if one's header names the current branch, it aborts with a message quoting the interrupted run's original prompt and the branch, telling the user to either resume the interrupted run (the shell's existing "Resume interrupted run" offer, which relies on the same progress-file mechanism) or switch branches.

To make the situation visible before the user even picks a menu item, the orca shell also gains a current-branch status line, printed above the main menu on every redraw (the branch can change between menu visits, since a flow run checks out branches) — at startup it lands right below the existing "agents:" and "stack:" summary lines. The progress-log scan is extracted from the shell's ResumeDetector into the shared `orca.progress` package so the runner-side check and the shell-side resume offer detect "run in progress" by the identical rules.

tasks.title: Extract shared progress-log scanning into orca.progress
tasks.description: Move the directory scan currently private to the shell's ResumeDetector into the flow module, e.g. `orca.progress.ProgressScan`: list every `.orca/progress-<12 hex>.json` under a workDir, preserving the existing guards — a symlinked or missing `.orca` root yields no candidates, individual symlinked files are excluded, filenames must match `progress-[0-9a-f]{12}\.json`. Suggested API: `def progressLogPaths(workDir: os.Path): List[os.Path]`, plus a convenience pairing each path with its cleanly-parsed header (via `ProgressStore.at(workDir, path).loadDetailed()`), silently skipping corrupt logs. Rework `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/resume/ResumeDetector.scala` to delegate its `newestProgressLogPath` scan to the helper; its newest-by-mtime pick and `fromHeader`/`isBareFlowFilename` filtering stay in the shell. Add a flow-module test (temp dir via `orca.testkit.TempDirs`: matching/non-matching filenames, symlinked file excluded, symlinked/missing `.orca` root); shell's existing resume tests must stay green. Behavior-preserving refactor — no user-visible change.

tasks.title: Abort a fresh flow run when another run is in progress on the current branch
tasks.description: In `FlowLifecycle.setup` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala), after `startBranch = git.currentBranch()` and BEFORE `session.applyCleanlinessPolicy()` (so the abort precedes any stash/branch/tree mutation — the check is read-only, so the pre-stash read is safe): when this run's own store is not `LoadResult.Loaded` (i.e. not a resume of the same prompt), scan progress logs via the shared helper, excluding the run's own `store.path`; if any cleanly-parsed header has `branch == startBranch`, throw `OrcaFlowException` (reporting the newest match by mtime when several qualify, consistent with ResumeDetector). The message must include: the interrupted run's original prompt (`header.userPrompt`, sanitized — control chars stripped, whitespace flattened, clipped — mirroring `MainMenu.taskPreview`, since the header is committed/untrusted content; a fallback like "(not recorded)" when None on a pre-feature log), the branch name, and guidance: resume the interrupted run (the orca shell's "Resume interrupted run" menu item, or re-run the same flow with the identical task text) or switch to a different branch first. Logs naming a different branch, and corrupt logs, never trigger the error. The check applies in both normal and skip-branch mode. Tests in runner FlowLifecycleTest: conflicting log on the current branch aborts with prompt+branch in the message and leaves tree/branch untouched (no stash); same-prompt resume still works; a log for another branch doesn't abort; a corrupt foreign log doesn't abort; `userPrompt = None` still aborts with the fallback text. Amend adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md with a short note on the new refusal.

tasks.title: Show the current git branch above the orca shell menu
tasks.description: In `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/ConfigSummary.scala` add `def branchLine(workDir: os.Path): Option[String]` rendering `branch: <name>` — a best-effort `os.proc("git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")` call in workDir (precedent: `shell/.../create/FlowCommit.scala` shells out to git directly). Return None (line omitted) when workDir is not a git repo or git fails; render detached HEAD (git reports the literal `HEAD`) explicitly, e.g. `branch: (detached HEAD)`. Print it in ONE place: `Main.loop`, re-evaluated via `ShellOutput.info` at the top of each iteration, right above the `ui.select` main-menu prompt — this covers startup too (the menu paints immediately after `printConfigSummary`, so the line lands next to the agents/stack lines) and stays fresh after a flow run changes the branch; do NOT also add it to `printConfigSummary`, which would duplicate the line at startup. Tests: ConfigSummaryTest covering a temp git repo on a named branch, a non-repo dir (None), and detached HEAD; a MainTest wiring check that the line appears above the menu. Mention the branch line in the ADR 0021 shell doc (and the README shell section only if it enumerates the startup summary lines).

resultJson.brief:
## Repo & build
Scala 3, direct-style (Ox). sbt multi-module; dependency chain relevant here: `tools` ← `flow` ← `runner` ← `shell`. Build/test: `sbt compile`, `sbt "flow/test"`, `sbt "runner/testOnly orca.runner.FlowLifecycleTest"`, `sbt scalafmtAll` before finishing. Tests are munit `FunSuite`; temp dirs via `orca.testkit.TempDirs.dir()`. sbt runs take 8–15 min — run builds in the background. NEVER commit unless asked. MANDATORY per CLAUDE.md: invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill (Skill tool) before writing/reviewing any Scala code. Comment style: scaladoc on non-obvious members about usage/invariants (never implementation history); inline comments only where non-trivial reasoning is needed; keep them local to file-specific facts. Ignore `.claude/worktrees/**` duplicates of source files.

## Key files
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/ProgressLog.scala` — `ProgressHeader(startingBranch: String, branch: String, promptHash: String, branchMode: BranchMode, userPrompt: Option[String] = None, flowName: Option[String] = None)`. `userPrompt`/`flowName` are None on logs written before the resume-offer feature; tolerant codec (`ProgressLog` given) round-trips across versions.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/ProgressStore.scala` — file lives at `.orca/progress-<hash>.json`, `hash` = first 12 hex chars of SHA-256(prompt) (`ProgressStore.hashPrompt`, private[orca]). `ProgressStore.default(workDir, prompt)` derives the path; `ProgressStore.at(workDir, path)` opens a known path (built for scanning). `loadDetailed(): LoadResult` = `Absent | Corrupt(reason) | Loaded(log)`.
- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/progress/RecoveryCheck.scala` — header validation on resume; treats the header as untrusted committed content. Follow this file's threat framing (untrusted header ⇒ sanitize anything echoed to the terminal), but note agents are trusted-but-fallible: justify checks by accident (merge carried log, hand edit), never by adversarial agents.
- `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala` — the heart of task 2. `setup(...)` sequence: `warnIfSettingsIgnored` → `startBranch = git.currentBranch()` → `snapshotLog` → `SetupSession.applyCleanlinessPolicy()` (stash/tolerate; skip-branch mode already does a throwaway pre-stash `store.loadDetailed()` peek — precedent for peeking before the stash) → `restoreLogIfMissing` → `resolveStackSettings` (may call the model) → `bindBranch` (the AUTHORITATIVE `loadDetailed()` read: Corrupt→warn+fresh, Absent→fresh, Loaded→`resumeBinding`, which validates the header via `RecoveryCheck.validateHeader` and cross-checks `git.currentBranch() == header.branch`, the "R30" check). The new conflict check goes between `startBranch` and the cleanliness policy; it fires only when the run's OWN store is not Loaded (Loaded = legit resume, handled downstream — do not error there even if other logs also name the branch). Throwing `OrcaFlowException` (from the `orca` package, already imported) is the abort idiom — `buildContext`'s `surfaced` wrapper in `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala` (~line 416) turns it into an `OrcaEvent.Error` on the event surface. `setup` already receives `store: ProgressStore` and `workDir: os.Path`, so it can both exclude `store.path` and scan workDir.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/resume/ResumeDetector.scala` — current owner of the scan to extract: `newestProgressLogPath` (symlink-guarded `os.list` of `OrcaDir.rootPath(workDir)`, filename regex `progress-[0-9a-f]{12}\.json`, excludes symlinked files, newest by `os.mtime`), all failures silent.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/Main.scala` — `loop(...)` is the tail-recursive menu redraw; it already re-evaluates `ResumeDetector.detect(os.pwd)` and `ManifestReader.list` on every redraw, so re-reading the branch each redraw is consistent and cheap. `printConfigSummary(globalSettingsPath, workDir)` prints `ConfigSummary.agentsLine` + `stackLine` via `ShellOutput.info` at startup and after Reconfigure/EditSettings — leave it unchanged; the branch line prints in `loop` only.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/ConfigSummary.scala` — `agentsLine`/`stackLine` return plain `String`s (`"agents: …"`, `"stack: …"`); errors render as one-line warnings, never crash. Match that tone: `branchLine` must be best-effort, no exceptions escaping.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/create/FlowCommit.scala` — precedent for shelling out: `os.proc("git" +: args).call(cwd = …, check = false, …)`-style. `GitTool`'s `OsGitTool(workDir, dispatcher)` needs an event dispatcher — not worth constructing in the shell for one read; use os.proc.
- `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/MainMenu.scala` — `taskPreview` (strip/flatten/`filterNot(_.isControl)`/clip) is the sanitization pattern to mirror when echoing a header-sourced prompt into the conflict error message.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaDir.scala` — `rootPath(workDir)` = `.orca/`, `progressPath(workDir, promptHash)`.
- `tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitTool.scala` — `currentBranch(): String` (returns literal `"HEAD"` when detached).

## Existing tests to extend / keep green
- `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala` (~3000 lines) — drives `FlowLifecycle.setup`/`readSettings` against real temp git repos; copy its fixture patterns (it avoids the developer's real `~/.config`).
- `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/resume/` — ResumeDetector tests; must pass unchanged after the scan extraction.
- `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/actions/ConfigSummaryTest.scala` and `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/MainTest.scala` — homes for the branch-line tests; MainTest already fakes UI (`ShellUi`) and injects seams (`workDir`, `spawnEditor` style params) — follow that injection convention rather than reading `os.pwd` untestably.

## Non-obvious facts
- The whole gap exists because progress files are prompt-keyed: same prompt ⇒ same file ⇒ resume path; different prompt ⇒ `Absent` ⇒ silent fresh run on whatever branch you're on. The branch match (`header.branch == git.currentBranch()`) is the conflict signal, mirroring `resumeBinding`'s R30 cross-check and ResumeDetector's presence-on-branch reasoning.
- Success teardown deletes the progress file (`teardownSuccess`); failure teardown keeps it and stays on the feature branch — so a progress file whose header names the current branch IS "run in progress on this branch". No PID/exit-code bookkeeping exists or is needed.
- Multiple progress files can coexist (different prompts, possibly one branch); ResumeDetector deliberately surfaces only the newest by mtime — the conflict check follows the same rule.
- The conflict check reads foreign logs pre-stash (possibly dirty content). That's acceptable because the check only aborts — it never takes destructive action, unlike `bindBranch`'s authoritative read, which must stay post-stash.
- ADRs live in `adr/`; the lifecycle contract is ADR 0018 (`0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md`), the shell is ADR 0021. Existing scaladoc cites ADR sections inline — keep that habit. Keep doc additions concise.
- `.orca/settings.properties` being committed is intentional; don't touch it.
- `ShellOutput.info` is the shell's plain info-line printer; the menu itself is `ui.select("orca shell", MainMenu.choices(...))`.
